ending: The Storm Kingdom wins the One Day War, also known as the War of Four Cities, but loses many experienced adventurers. Dawn expends her sole direct intervention to erase the Builder's land city, the submarine kraken city is defeated, and the flying fortress falls after Liara Rimaros delivers the true destructive device to its core. Vesper Rimaros and Liara's brother die enabling that strike. Divine and water-essence intervention turns the falling fortress into an island and saves Liveros. A month later, Jason's reunited team is operating as a portal-enabled response force during the still-active monster surge. Jason remains silver rank and cannot revive again until gold rank. Arabelle Remore helps him face his fear that his changed self has lost his friends' trust, and every team member proves otherwise by entering his spirit vault. The local Builder cult is largely cleared, but the worldwide Builder war, Purity's conversion campaign, the Messengers, and the damaged route to Earth remain unresolved.
in_short: Jason Asano and Farrah Hurin return from Earth during an extreme monster surge and become entangled in the Storm Kingdom's defense against the Builder. While Jason undertakes isolated supply missions and survives attacks engineered through Purity, his former companions disrupt a Purity ritual that brings Earth outworlders and interdimensional Messengers into the world. Jason's involvement in royal politics and Builder operations exposes both his dangerous new powers and his deteriorating judgment. His friends finally reach Rimaros, and the reunited team joins the kingdom's rapid-response effort. When multiple Builder cities attack, Dawn destroys the land city and local forces defeat the submarine city. Liara Rimaros carries a locally made weapon into a surprise flying fortress; Vesper Rimaros and Liara's brother die securing its destruction, while divine intervention saves Liveros from the fall. One month later, Jason's team remains active in the surge, and their entry into his spirit vault demonstrates that their trust in him has survived.

recaps.text: Previously: Jason Asano was taken from Earth to Palomustus, became an adventurer, and built a close team around friends including Humphrey, Sophie, Belinda, Clive, Rufus, Farrah, and Gary. His conflicts with the Builder left him implanted with a starseed that failed to control him and eventually gave him unusual influence over Builder magic. Jason and Farrah were believed dead after events returned them to Earth, where Jason was reborn through a World Phoenix token. Their companions remained on Palomustus without certainty that either had survived. Jason's time on Earth transformed his spirit realm and involved him in an unfinished effort to connect the two worlds safely.

Jason and Farrah leave Earth through a standing-stone ritual, carrying Jason's evolved spirit realm along the World Phoenix bridge. On Palomustus, Dawn tells Jason's former companions that the pair survived and warns that their return will coincide with an abnormally severe monster surge and a Builder war. Gary and Virid Martin reforge Jason's damaged soul-bonded sword as Hegemon's Will. The surge begins as Jason's separated team encounters a newly manifested floating Builder city and captures one of its pursuing skyships. Jason and Farrah emerge into a cyclone in the Sea of Storms, reach the Storm Kingdom with Shade's help, and head for Rimaros to register for surge duty. Their attempt to stay unnoticed is complicated by official records listing them as dead and by Jason's suspicious aura disguise. At Liveros, Jason senses Rufus nearby before he can complete the registration process.

Jason and Farrah reunite with Rufus and obtain Temple of Death certification of their identities. Adventure Society scrutiny sends Jason to the Builder Response Unit, where a soul-projection test provokes imprisoned starseeds and clockwork cores. Liara Rimaros concludes that Jason is an anti-Builder asset rather than an agent, but keeps him under observation. Jason, Farrah, and Rufus establish a cloud-house base beside an Arnot waterfall, and Jason restores Gordon to his familiar team. Meanwhile, Humphrey's group learns that Jason and Farrah are alive but must complete an anti-Purity mission before travelling to them. Jason also discovers why members of the royal family recognized his name: Zara Rimaros falsely presented him as a prospective husband, then used his reported death to avoid an arranged marriage. An unnamed diamond-rank Rimaros royal asks Jason to remain inconspicuous while the family contains the political damage. Jason agrees on the condition that the separated companions and Farrah's family are eventually brought to Rimaros.

Jason accepts solitary supply work during the monster surge while the royal family covertly evaluates him. Melody Jane appears as a powerful defender at a remote fortress despite signs of a Purity connection. Soromir places the gold-rank Trenchant Moore aboard Jason's supply ship to judge his strength and conduct. Jason detects the test, defeats a large flock of silver-rank flying monsters without revealing the full extent of his abilities, and insists that he will cooperate only if the royals avoid making a spectacle of him. In parallel, Humphrey's team begins an operation against a hidden Purity stronghold. Jason reaches a gorge fortress under attack by intelligent Bone Feasters and fights the horde alone. He uses his familiars, afflictions, and large-scale life drains to survive, then converts the accumulated conditions into decisive damage and clears the remaining monsters. With the Bone Feasters defeated, Jason approaches the fortress ward and identifies himself as its expected courier.

Jason continues his delivery circuit while hidden observers follow him. At an isolated fortress, Melody Jane's Purity faction engineers a supply crisis so desperate defenders will accept redeemed cores, sacrificing their former abilities and freedom for an immediate rise in rank. Humphrey's team finds Builder constructs guarding the Purity dam and disrupts its regulator when the original sabotage plan becomes impossible. The resulting portal collapse devastates the hidden valley and strands 119 outworlders. Investigators identify the winged arrivals as interdimensional Messengers and discover that the ritual was powered by the sacrifice of Purity adherents' families. Three Purity loyalists then ambush Jason with equipment tailored to counter his movement, familiars, and afflictions. Liara and her gold-rank teammates have used his exposed route to seek a cult base, but Jason forces them to intervene rather than let him be captured. They take the attackers alive. Jason survives badly depleted, confronts Liara over using him as bait, and learns that Builder restrictions are forcing its allies to target him indirectly.

Jason returns to Rimaros and chooses to understand the royal crisis before acting. Taika, one of the new Earth outworlders, meets Jason's former team and confirms that many arrivals know Jason's story. Vesper and Liara prepare a public account that will preserve the alliance with House Irios while recasting Zara's supposed attachment to Jason as youthful error. Jason learns that Zara invented the claim to protect Caspar Irios, whose own relationship made him unwilling to accept their arranged match. Jason tells Caspar the truth directly and sends him to address his family. Soromir reveals that he deliberately left a Builder beacon intact and believes it drew Jason and Farrah to the Storm Kingdom so Purity proxies could kill Jason without violating the Builder's compact. That compact limits overwhelming attacks on Jason unless he first interferes. Meanwhile, Rufus considers devoting himself to teaching, Farrah finally contacts her parents, and Jason's combat record leads Trenchant to classify him as an affliction skirmisher suited to dangerous, highly mobile fights rather than conventional formations.

Liara acknowledges that the royal family has treated Jason as a tool and begins dealing with him more directly. Farrah warns Soromir that Jason is nearing a psychological breaking point and secures a promise that his team will be brought to Rimaros. Before that can happen, Jason joins a rushed expedition to a Builder-held astral aperture despite Shade's warning that he is not fit for the mission. He slips away, takes control of bronze-rank Builder clockwork, disrupts stronger constructs, and uses cultists' starseeds against them. Inside the aperture, he captures five cultists and nearly tears apart one prisoner's body-soul connection until Shade stops him. Jason opens the way for the expedition, whose members reject the Builder's offer to withdraw in exchange for killing him. The Builder reveals that Jason cannot return from another death until he reaches gold rank. Jason admits that he no longer trusts his own judgment. As the expedition returns with prisoners, Dawn arrives in Rimaros carrying Jason's former companions, associates, and family connections, placing the long-delayed reunion within reach.

Jason reunites with Humphrey, Sophie, Belinda, Gary, Clive, Neil, Taika, Travis, Arabelle, Farrah's parents, and the rest of his waiting circle. He accepts Humphrey and Sophie's relationship, admits that he is psychologically unwell, and receives the completed Regalia of the Dark Hegemon from Gary. Taika and Travis explain that the unstable Earth rift destroyed their bodies and delivered their souls to Palomustus as outworlders. Clive concludes that the rift intersected with the disrupted Purity summoning, producing more than one hundred such arrivals. Jason intends to build a safe route back, although the work will take years. His companions register together and begin supply and rapid-response contracts across the Storm Kingdom. The Builder then declares open war. Two massive cities approach, leaving the kingdom without enough diamond-rank defenders. Dawn is permitted only one direct intervention and must also preserve Jason for a future interworld task. Jason's willingness to sacrifice himself forces her to help, while Travis, Clive, Gary, and their collaborators begin adapting an Earth weapon concept for use against Builder forces.

Dawn keeps Jason on Arnot while his companions deploy against the approaching Builder cities. Jason helps defend the lightly guarded island and defeats a gold-rank wraith giant alone, confirming how dangerous the gap between silver and gold remains. When the Builder's submarine city surfaces as a colossal kraken construct, the kingdom's main force attacks it. Pirates exploit the mobilization to raid Casilaro, but Peli engages their gold-rank captain while Jason defeats and captures members of the crew. Dawn then spends her one intervention to destroy the advancing land city. A third threat immediately appears: a flying fortress over Liveros. Soromir organizes the defense around false devices and one real weapon. Farrah completes a ritual beneath the city while Rufus and Gary protect her, allowing adventurers to enter. Liara carries the real device toward the core. Vesper dies holding off defenders, and Liara's brother remains behind to conceal and trigger the weapon. The fortress falls, but the churches divert it into the sea and suppress the resulting wave, saving Liveros at the cost of severe adventurer losses.

One month after the One Day War, the Storm Kingdom has defeated all three Builder cities that entered its territory. Dawn erased the land city, the submarine kraken city was sunk, and the fallen flying fortress has become a new island southwest of Liveros. Vesper Rimaros, Liara's brother, and many other adventurers are dead. The reduced ranks force larger quotas and less conservative assignments while the monster surge continues. Jason's reunited team works repeated supply, fortress-support, and Builder-cult cleanup contracts through his expanding portal network. The local Builder cult has largely been removed from the Sea of Storms, but the Builder remains a worldwide threat and other regions have suffered far worse. Jason is still silver rank and cannot revive again before reaching gold. Arabelle helps him identify fear of rejection as a central obstacle in his recovery. Jason finally allows the team into his spirit vault, a place that admits others only through deep trust, and every member enters. Their choice confirms that his friends still trust the person he has become.
